structure: Rhode Island Social Studies Standards (2023), one PDF; this part covers Grade 7 (from SS7.6.2), Grade 8, and HS Civics, US History I, US History II, World History I (to SSHS.WHI.4.3). Each grade/course opens with a heading unit (e.g. 'GRADE 8 - ...', 'HIGH SCHOOL - CIVICS') followed by a narrative and a list of Inquiry Topics, Compelling Questions and standard codes/titles. Then 'Standards Tables': an 'Inquiry Topic N: ... Compelling Question' heading, followed by one table per standard. Codes: SS<grade>.<topic>.<n> for grades (SS7.6.2), SSHS.<course>.<topic>.<n> for HS (CVC=Civics, USI, USII, WHI). Each standard table has: header cell with code + title + standard statement (the code/title/statement text is split across units because of cell layout, interleaved with the 'Connections to the Rhode Island Anchor Standards' label, anchor-standard code cells CG.P, CG.RL, CG.RR, H.CC, H.HP, H.IG, G.HPE, G.HSP, G.WST, E.SA, E.PC, E.EG and 'X' marks showing which anchors are connected); then 'Guiding Questions for Instruction' (bulleted questions; examples) and 'Learning Assessment Objectives: Students demonstrate an ability to: a. ... b. ...' (detailed performance expectations with e.g. lists; labeled standards). Table index [T1 R.. C..] is positional, not grade columns: each standard table is a single-grade/course table. Rare [T2 ...] fragments are overflow text continuing the preceding GQ/LAO cell across a page break. Grade 7 = SS7.x (world history), Grade 8 = SS8.x (civics); HS courses are 9-12 with course title as in the heading.
